overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 6
overview.text: In this lesson, students develop a deep conceptual and procedural understanding of Exponential Growth—U.S. Population and World Population in Module 3: Linear and Exponential Functions.
outcomes: Students compare linear and exponential models of population growth.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 6 Exit Ticket: Exponential Growth—U.S. Population and World Population
exitTicket.prompt:
Exit Ticket

Do the examples below require a linear or exponential growth model? State whether each example is linear or exponential, and write an explicit formula for the sequence that models the growth for each case. Include a description of the variables you use.

A savings account accumulates no interest but receives a deposit of $825 per month.

The value of a house increases by 1.5% per year.

Every year, the alligator population is \frac{9}{7} of the previous year's population.

The temperature increases by 2° every 30 minutes from 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. each day for the month of July.

Every 240 minutes, \frac{1}{3} of the rodent population dies.
exitTicket.solution:
Do the examples below require a linear or exponential growth model? State whether each example is linear or exponential, and write an explicit formula for the sequence that models the growth for each case. Include a description of the variables you use.

A savings account accumulates no interest but receives a deposit of $825 per month.

Linear; f(t)=825t, where f(t) represents the accumulated value in the account after t months

The value of a house increases by 1.5% per year.

Exponential; f(t)=b(1.015)^{t}, where b represents the beginning value of the house and f(t) is the value of the house after t years

Every year, the alligator population is \frac{9}{7} of the previous year's population.

Exponential; P(t)=c(\frac{9}{7})^{t}, where c represents the current population of alligators and P(t) is the alligator population after t years

The temperature increases by 2° every 30 minutes from 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. each day for the month of July.

Linear; T(t)=2t+b, where b represents the beginning temperature and T(t) is the temperature after t half-hour periods since 8:00 a.m.

Every 240 minutes, \frac{1}{3} of the rodent population dies.

Exponential; r(t)=p(\frac{2}{3})^{t}, where p is the current population of rodents and r(t) is the remaining population of rodents after t four-hour periods

problemSet.title: Official Worksheet: Problem Set & Practice
problemSet.description: Master Exponential Growth—U.S. Population and World Population through authentic curriculum practice problems. Check your work using the expandable teacher solution key below.

problems.prompt:
Student Friendly Bank pays a simple interest rate of 2.5% per year. Neighborhood Bank pays a compound interest rate of 2.1% per year, compounded monthly.

Which bank will provide the largest balance if you plan to invest $10,000 for 10 years? For 20 years?
problems.solution: Student Friendly Bank gives a larger balance at the 10-year mark. Neighborhood Bank gives a larger balance by the 20-year mark.

problems.prompt: Write an explicit formula for the sequence that models the balance in the Student Friendly Bank account t years after a deposit is left in the account.
Write an explicit formula for the sequence that models the balance in the Neighborhood Bank account m months after a deposit is left in the account.

Create a table of values indicating the balances in the two bank accounts from year 2 to year 20 in 2-year increments. Round each value to the nearest dollar.

Which bank is a better short-term investment? Which bank is better for those leaving money in for a longer period of time? When are the investments about the same?
problems.solution: Student Friendly Bank; Neighborhood Bank; they are about the same by the end of year 17.

problems.prompt: What type of model is Student Friendly Bank? What is the rate or ratio of change?
What type of model is Neighborhood Bank? What is the rate or ratio of change?

The table below represents the population of the state of New York for the years 1800—2000. Use this information to answer the questions.

Using the year 1800 as the base year, an explicit formula for the sequence that models the population of New York is P(t)=300 000(1.021)^{t}, where t is the number of years after 1800.
Using this formula, calculate the projected population of New York in 2010.
Using the Internet (or some other source), find the population of the state of New York according to the 2010 census. Which formula yielded a more accurate prediction of the 2010 population?
problems.solution: The actual population of the state of New York in 2010 was 19,200,000. The formula in part (b) resulted in a more accurate prediction.
